sections.h2: Where do you record a deed in Kalamazoo County?
sections.html:
Deeds for Kalamazoo County land are recorded at the Register of Deeds in the County Administration Building, 201 West Kalamazoo Avenue, Kalamazoo, MI 49007. The phone number is 269-383-8970. The county describes the register of deeds as a constitutional office created in 1835, and says recording makes a document public without making it legally valid.

Staff there index and keep the records, and they do not search titles or give legal advice. For a house sale in Kalamazoo County, your title company usually handles the trip or sends the deed electronically. A seller who is doing the paperwork alone should still read the checklist below, since the counter rejects documents that miss a formatting rule.

Kalamazoo County has four cities (Galesburg, Kalamazoo, Parchment and Portage) and five villages (Augusta, Climax, Richland, Schoolcraft and Vicksburg), according to Wikipedia. All of them record at this single office.

sections.h2: What are the recording fees in Kalamazoo County?
sections.html:
Recording a document costs $30, as the county fee schedule states under MCL 600.2567. Extra charges apply in a few cases:

  • $3 for each additional instrument when one document assigns or discharges more than one.
  • $1 per page for copies and $5 per document to certify one.
  • $5 per search for a file or record search done by staff.
  • $5 for a tax certificate covering up to 20 tax ID numbers on one document, then 20 cents for each added description.

The county accepts cash, checks, money orders and cards. Make recording checks payable to the Kalamazoo County Register of Deeds, and make tax certificate checks payable to the treasurer involved. The county FAQ says there is no online payment portal, so card payments go through the office phone line or the counter. You can see the full amounts in the county fee schedule.

sections.h2: How is transfer tax figured in Kalamazoo County?
sections.html:
The county collects transfer tax from the seller when the deed is recorded, at $1.10 per $1,000 for the county and $7.50 per $1,000 for the state. The county rounds the price up to the next $500 first, so a house that sold for $100,000.01 is taxed as $100,500.

Those figures match the statutory rates of 55 cents and $3.75 per $500. The county rate sits in MCL 207.504, and the state act names the seller as the person who owes the tax in MCL 207.523.

Combined transfer tax by price, from the Kalamazoo County fee schedule rates

$100,000$110$750$860
$242,000$266.20$1,815$2,081.20
$350,000$385$2,625$3,010

The middle row uses the Census median value of $241,800, rounded up to $242,000. The county has a transfer tax chart on its website for other prices, and it lists exemptions for both the county and state taxes.

sections.h2: Which Kalamazoo County deeds need a tax certificate?
sections.html:
Any deed that says the grantor "warrants" or "defends" the title needs a tax clearance from the treasurer before recording. The county lists warranty deeds, covenant deeds, land contracts, assignments of land contract with a warranty clause, master deeds and amended master deeds that add property to a condominium. The statute behind the rule is MCL 211.135.

A house inside the City of Kalamazoo has one extra step. The seller first obtains a city tax certificate from the City Treasurer at Kalamazoo City Hall, 241 W South Street, phone 269-337-8036, for a $10 fee. Only then does the County Treasurer issue the county certificate. Skipping the city step delays the county one.

If taxes are unpaid, the treasurer will not clear the parcel, and the closing has to pay the balance first. Ask the treasurer for a payoff figure early, since interest accrues monthly on delinquent balances.

sections.h2: What does the Kalamazoo County register of deeds require on a document?
sections.html:
The page layout must follow MCL 565.201, and the county FAQ turns those rules into a short list. Bring a document that meets every item:

  • Page size from 8.5 by 11 to 8.5 by 14 inches on white paper of 20 pound weight.
  • Black ink with type of at least 10 points.
  • A 2.5 inch blank band across the top of page one, with the document type on the first line of print at or below that band, and half inch margins elsewhere.
  • A notary for the deed types the county lists, including warranty, quitclaim, executor, trustee and sheriff's deeds. Witnesses are no longer required.
  • Court documents certified and sealed by the court.

A rejected document comes back with a letter naming the reasons. Fix them and resubmit. If the office asks you to prepare a new deed to add or remove a name, hire an attorney or a title agency, since staff cannot draft it.

sections.h2: Can I record a Kalamazoo County deed electronically?
sections.html:
Yes, through four certified vendors: CSC, ePN, Indecomm and Simplifile. The county accepts these filings during business hours on weekdays that are not county holidays, takes payment by ACH under the vendor agreements, and warns that vendors can add their own processing fees. Plats and master deeds with full size maps are not accepted for e-recording.

Michigan adopted statewide e-recording standards effective January 1, 2014, and the county ties its rules to them. Most sellers never deal with a vendor directly, since the title company submits the deed.

There is also a Consumer E-Recording portal for one time filers. It takes affidavits, discharges, mortgages, certificates of trust, liens and releases, but the county says deeds and other ownership transfers, UCC documents and foreclosure papers are not eligible. A seller recording a deed by hand should plan to use the counter or a title company.

sections.h2: How do I find a recorded deed in Kalamazoo County?
sections.html:
Use the Document Searches page on the county site. The Deeds Search tool has no charge to search the index, though viewing, printing or saving a document costs $1 per page plus a processing fee. Tapestry EON, offered since October 21, 2024, charges $8.75 per search, and Laredo is a monthly subscription for regular users such as title professionals.

Staff will also look up a deed for you for $5 per property plus $1 per page, and certify it for another $5. Public workstations in the Administration Building are free to search, with a $1 per page charge for prints. Searching by name works better than by address, because an address is not required on recorded papers.

The county says land record images go back to 1831, while a complete index covers 1984 forward. For older chains of title, a title company search is the safer route.

sections.h2: How does Kalamazoo County compare on housing?
sections.html:
Kalamazoo County has a larger renter share than neighboring Jackson or Kalkaska counties, which shapes who sells and who buys. The Census Bureau's QuickFacts table reports 263,795 people in mid 2025, 116,117 housing units and a 64.5 percent owner occupied rate for 2020 to 2024.

  • Median value of an owner occupied home: $241,800.
  • Median household income: $72,532 in 2024 dollars.
  • Median gross rent: $1,093 a month.
  • Bachelor's degree or higher among adults 25 and older: 41.3 percent.

Wikipedia notes that the county covers 562 square miles of land, that I-94 crosses its middle, and that US 131 runs north and south through its west central part. Sellers outside the city limits deal with the same recording office but a township or village treasurer for local tax questions.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Kalamazoo County?
faqs.a: It costs $30 per document. Transfer tax and a tax certificate are separate charges, and a document that assigns or discharges several instruments adds $3 for each extra one.

faqs.q: Do I pay transfer tax as the seller in Kalamazoo County?
faqs.a: Yes. The seller owes it, and it is paid to the Register of Deeds when the deed is recorded. The county rate is $1.10 per $1,000 and the state rate is $7.50 per $1,000, using a price rounded up to the next $500.

faqs.q: Does a Kalamazoo city home need two tax certificates?
faqs.a: Yes. A property inside the City of Kalamazoo needs a $10 city certificate from the City Treasurer first, then the county certificate, which costs $5 for up to 20 tax ID numbers.

faqs.q: Does a Kalamazoo County deed need witnesses?
faqs.a: No. The county says witnesses are no longer required, but warranty deeds, quitclaim deeds and most other deed types do need a notary.

faqs.q: Can I pay Kalamazoo County recording fees by card?
faqs.a: Yes, by calling the office at 269-383-8970 or paying at the counter at 201 West Kalamazoo Avenue. The county has no online payment portal for counter recordings.
